page: Amazon Web Services m8idn.2xlarge is an eighth-generation general-purpose compute instance built on the AWS Nitro hypervisor architecture. The instance runs on an Intel x86_64 processor clocked at 3.9 GHz, providing 8 vCPUs derived from 4 dedicated physical cores with 2 threads per core. System memory is configured at 32 GB of RAM, sustaining a 1:4 core-to-memory ratio of 4 GB per virtual core. The platform integrates 12 Gbps of baseline network bandwidth alongside network and EBS optimization, while operating without dedicated GPU hardware or complimentary public IPv4 addresses.

A primary distinction of this instance type is the inclusion of 474 GB of bundled local NVMe SSD instance storage. This hardware configuration supplies direct, low-latency disk throughput without relying solely on remote block storage volumes. From an architectural perspective, the presence of dedicated hardware threads combined with local solid-state drives delivers higher cost efficiency for I/O-intensive services compared to instances requiring separately provisioned high-IOPS network storage. Because instance store storage is ephemeral by nature, workloads requiring long-term state persistence must implement external replication or backups to persistent storage layers.

Given the balance of dedicated 3.9 GHz Intel CPU cores, 32 GB RAM, 12 Gbps baseline networking, and high-speed local NVMe storage, the m8idn.2xlarge is suited for mid-sized relational and NoSQL databases, transactional processing, and cache layers such as Redis or Memcached. The high-throughput local disk and network capacity also match the operational needs of continuous integration pipelines, ETL batch data transformations, and high-traffic web applications that process substantial temporary file volumes.
description: Amazon Web Services m8idn.2xlarge is an eighth-generation general-purpose instance powered by the Nitro hypervisor and Intel x86_64 architecture. It provides 8 vCPUs across 4 dedicated physical cores operating at 3.9 GHz, accompanied by 32 GB of system memory, matching a standard 1:4 compute-to-memory distribution. Network performance features a 12 Gbps baseline throughput with network and EBS optimization. The instance includes 474 GB of direct-attached local NVMe SSD instance storage, enabling high-throughput and low-latency disk I/O without the immediate overhead of attached network volumes. While the ephemeral nature of the bundled storage requires external handling for stateful recovery, the combination of dedicated compute cores and onboard NVMe capacity yields favorable operational efficiency for data processing tasks. The m8idn.2xlarge is suited for relational and key-value databases, caching nodes, continuous integration systems, data analytics pipelines, and transactional web backend workloads.
